question.problem: Find $k$, if $u=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9} \\ \frac{k}{9} \\ -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}]$ is a unit vector.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{{u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{k}{9})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{(\frac{8}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{81}+\frac{{k}^{2}}{81}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{64}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{74+{k}^{2}}{81}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖u‖=1,$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{74+{k}^{2}}{81}} & =1 \\ \sqrt{74+{k}^{2}} & =9 \\ {(\sqrt{74+{k}^{2}})}^{2} & ={9}^{2} \\ 74+{k}^{2} & =81 \\ {k}^{2} & =7 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$
